correctness.rationale: The one-vector orthogonal projection has squared residual ab(X+Y)/(aX+bY), with a=σ1²>b=σ2²>0 and X,Y the positive squared coordinates. Put U=X/(X+Y); exchangeability gives E U=1/2. The strictly convex function ab/(b+(a-b)u) gives the lower bound 2ab/(a+b), with equality only if U=1/2 almost surely. Independent, identically distributed X and Y equal almost surely must be constant (every measurable threshold event has probability equal to its square); unit variance and centering then force iid fair signs. Gaussian polar coordinates make the angle uniform; quadrant substitution t=tan θ gives expected residual (2ab/π) times the integral from 0 to infinity of 1/(a+bt²), hence √(ab). Division yields (κ+κ⁻¹)/2, and κ→infinity proves noncomparability in the stated mean-squared sense. If a=b there is no strict optimizer, as the source notes. The singular-basis alignment, no oversampling, and squared norm are essential to the stated comparison. The supplied spot-check script and its reported 5316 cases were inspected as evidence, not executed; the audit uses exact derivations.
residual_risks: No numerical replay or formal verification is claimed; the theorem concerns only the aligned one-vector, two-mode model.
